title: Straight-line group-operation certificates need about log r / (2 log log r) operations
question:
Let G=

have order r. A straight-line program of length L is a_0=P, a_i = e1 a_j + e2 a_l with j,l < i and e1,e2 in {+1,-1}. At most 4^L (L!)^2 elements are outputs of such programs, so if 4^L (L!)^2 < r some Q in G has no SLP of length <= L. Consequently, if each group operation costs at least c*b bit operations (b = field bit length), verifying a worst-case instance by any SLP costs Omega(b^2/log b) bit operations, which is omega(n log n).
rationale: Registered by PI from sealed round-1 submissions before cross-agent synthesis or review.

notes: Origin: C2 (RUN-9eae1ad9). Restricted model only (SLP verifier); not a Turing-machine lower bound. | ECDLP-5: flaw found. 4^L(L!)^2 counts programs of length exactly L, while the claim is about length <= L (fixable: sum over i). The counting bound is strictly weaker than the trivial coefficient bound |n_i| <= 2^i (HYP-57d71f43). The consequence omega(n log n) bit cost depends on an unjustified per-operation cost assumption and holds only in a black-box SLP model; it is not a Turing-machine statement. Counting numerics L0(2^256)=29, L0(2^521)=50 reproduced.
